# schedule time zone

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:scheduleTimeZone`](gmeow-scheduleTimeZone.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/scheduleTimeZone>
- **Category:** property
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/calendar`](../../slices/calendar.md)
- **Box roles:** [RBox role](../boxes/rbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

The time zone in which this schedule's recurrence is expressed. The occurrence generation engine uses this zone when expanding the rule.

## Structure

**Property shape:** object property; [`gmeow:EventSchedule`](../classes/gmeow-EventSchedule.md) -> [`gmeow:TimeZone`](../classes/gmeow-TimeZone.md); functional

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:scheduleTimeZone`](gmeow-scheduleTimeZone.md) from [`gmeow:EventSchedule`](../classes/gmeow-EventSchedule.md) to [`gmeow:TimeZone`](../classes/gmeow-TimeZone.md) when the relationship itself belongs in the native GMEOW graph.

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use to fix the IANA zone a recurrence rule expands in — the offset that decides where each occurrence's local wall-clock time falls across DST boundaries.

### Avoid when

- Avoid asserting two zones (it is functional — one per schedule) and avoid omitting it for a wall-clock-anchored rule, since the expansion is ambiguous without the zone.

### How to use

- Set one [`gmeow:TimeZone`](../classes/gmeow-TimeZone.md); the engine reads it when turning the [`gmeow:scheduleRecurrenceRule`](gmeow-scheduleRecurrenceRule.md) into dated [`gmeow:scheduleOccurrence`](gmeow-scheduleOccurrence.md) events.

### Examples

- ex:standupSchedule [`gmeow:scheduleTimeZone`](gmeow-scheduleTimeZone.md) ex:torontoZone.
